## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

The *Wéimó jīng wúwǒ shū* (X0348) is a twelve-fascicle late-Ming Tiantai commentary on the *Vimalakīrti* by Yúyǒu [傳燈](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%82%B3%E7%87%88) Chuándēng (1554–1628 CE), the great late-Ming reviver of Tiantai Buddhism. The title's *wúwǒ* 無我 ("no-self") emphasizes the *Vimalakīrti*'s anātman doctrine and its convergence with Tiantai's threefold-truth (三諦) doctrine.

**Abstract**

Chuándēng (1554–1628 CE) was the leading Tiantai master of the late Ming and the founder of Yúyǒu sì 幽溪寺 in Tiantai. He is credited with reviving the Tiantai *xíngfǎ* (ritual practice) tradition and producing a substantial commentarial corpus. He was the teacher of [受登](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%8F%97%E7%99%BB) Shòudēng (who compiled the *Yàoshī sānmèi xíngfǎ* [KR6i0057](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0057)) and many other late-Ming and early-Qīng Tiantai figures.

The *Wúwǒ shū* is one of his major sūtra commentaries, applying Tiantai *yīniàn sānqiān* and *sāndì yuánróng* doctrines systematically to the *Vimalakīrti*. Together with [KR6i0103](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0103) (Yáng Qǐyuán's *Píng zhù*) and [KR6i0105](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6i/KR6i0105) (the anonymous *Wéimó jīng shū kē*), it represents the late-Ming Tiantai-tradition reception of the *Vimalakīrti*.

The catalog meta dates the work as Ming; Chuándēng's working life ran 1574–1628, with this *shū* falling in his mature period (after 1600).
